Sub: Outcome of Meeting of the Board of Directors held on Thursday, November 12, 2026.
Sir/Madam,
Pursuant to the Regulation 30 and 33 of the SEBI (LODR) Regulations, 2015, (“SEBI Regulations”),
the Board of Directors of the Company, at its meeting held today i.e., Thursday, November 12, 2026,
has inter-alia considered and approved the Unaudited Financial Results (Standalone & Consolidated)
for the quarter and half year ended on September 30, 2026 along with the Limited Review Report
(after being reviewed and recommended by the Audit Committee).
ln view of above, please find enclosed herewith a copy of the Integrated Financial Results
(Standalone & Consolidated) for the quarter and half year ended on September 30, 2026 along with
the Limited Review Report.
The aforesaid results are also being made available on the website of the Company i.e.
www.irctc.com
The Board meeting commenced at 03.00 P.M. and concluded at 04:45 P.M.
This is for your information and record please.
Thanking you,
Yours faithfully,
For and on behalf of
Indian Railway Catering & Tourism Corporation Limited
(Suman Kalra)
Company Secretary and Compliance Officer

3 InlinewithRailwayBoardCommercialCircularNo.CC-60of2019onincreaseincateringtariffforpost-paidandpre-paidtrains,

demandsbeforeHighCourtsorinvokedarbitration.AwardspassedagainsttheCompanyinsomecaseshavebeenchallenged

As the matter is sub-judice, the enhanced licence fee for the periods 18th November 2019 to 22nd March 2020 (post-paid

4 Asperthetermsandconditionsofthetender,inrespectofthefourPPPRailneerplants,theDeveloper-cum-Operators(DCOs)
aretobereimbursedtheGSTonthesupplyofRailneer,netoftheInputTaxCredit(ITC)availedbythem.However,complete
informationregardingtheITCavailedbytheDCOsisnotavailable.BasedontheinformationmadeavailablebycertainDCOs,an
amountof₹99.32lakhsand₹192.00lakhshasbeenaccountedforasaclaimbytheCompanytowardsITCforthequarterand
half year ended 30 September 2026, respectively, and an amount of ₹ 397.86 lakhs was accounted for during FY 2025-26.
Accordingly,thetotalamountaccountedforinthebooksoftheCompanyaggregatesto₹1847.30lakhsand₹2039.30lakhsas
at 31 March 2026 and 30 September 2026, respectively. The DCOs have contested the Company's claim towards ITC.
Themanagementhasissuedlettersto theDCOs directingthemtofurnishGSTR data,soas toenableIRCTCtoascertainthe
actual ITC availed by them. Based on such data, recovery of ITC shall be affected strictly in accordance with the contract
conditions.
TheDCOsofSankrail,Hapur&NagpurplantshavechallengedthesamebeforetheHon’bleCourt.IncaseofSankrailPlant,the
Hon’ble Delhi High Court has appointed an Arbitrator andrestrained theCompany from takingany recovery related stepsin
respectofanyamountpertainingtotheallegedinputtaxcredituntilthelearnedSoleArbitratortakesuptheapplicationunder
Section 17 for consideration. Similarly, in respect of Hapur and Nagpur plants, the matter are under arbitration before a
commonSoleArbitratorfortheseDCOs.IncaseofParassalaPlant,contracthasbeenterminatedandanoticeofdisputehas
already been issued. Necessary action will be taken in accordance with the concession agreement of Parassala Plant.
5 TheNational Anti-ProfiteeringAuthority(NAA)hadissuedanoticedated25February,2022 allegingprofiteering of₹5041.44
lakhunderCGSTAct,2017foronaccountofnon-passingthebenefitoftaxreductiontoconsumers.Theshowcausenoticewas
contested bytheCompany; however,noorderwaspassedbytheAuthority.Subsequently,CompetitionCommission ofIndia
(CCI) was empowered to adjudicate the matter. The matter was taken up by the Principal bench of the Hon'ble Goods & Services
Tax Appellate Tribunal (GSTAT).
The Hon'ble GSTAT, vide its judgment dated 14 October 2026, has passed an order against the Company in relation to
proceedingsunderSection171oftheCGSTAct,2017,concerningallegedprofiteeringinrespectofRailNeerpackageddrinking
water.TheHon'bleTribunalhasacceptedtheDGAPreportdated11June2021anddirectedtheCompanytodepositthealleged
profiteeredamountof₹5,041.44lakhintheCentralandStateConsumerWelfareFundsintheprescribedratioof50:50,along
withinterest@18%perannumfrom28June2019tillthedateofdeposit.Further,theTribunalhasimposedapenalty@10%of
theprofiteered amount with theprovision thatthepenaltyshallnot be payableif theentire profiteered amount along with
applicableinterestisdepositedwithin30daysfromthedateoftheorder.Theappealtothesaidorderisbeingpreferredbefore
the Competent court of jurisdiction.
A provision amounting to ₹11,629.85 lakh has been recognised during quarter and half year ended 30 September 2026 and
disclosedasanexceptionaliteminthefinancialresults.Theprovisionincludestheallegedprofiteeredamountof₹5,041.44and
interest @18% per annum up to 30 September 2026.

Independent Auditor's Review Report on quarterly and year to date unaudited standalone financial
results of the Company Pursuant to the regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligation and Disclosure
Requirements) Regulations, 2015, as amended
Review Report to
The Board of Directors
Indian Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited
1. We have reviewed the accompanying Statement of unaudited standalone financial results of Indian
Railway Catering and Tourism Corporation Limited ("the Company") for the quarter and half year ended
September 30, 2026 (“the Statement”), being submitted by the Company pursuant to the requirements
of Regulation 33 of the SEBI (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 as
amended (the “Listing Regulations”).
2. The Statement, which is the responsibility of the Company's Management and approved by the
Company's Board of Directors, has been prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement
principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34, “Interim Financial Reporting” (“Ind AS 34”),
prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act, 2013 (“the Act”), read with relevant rules issued
thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India and is in compliance with the
presentation and disclosure requirements of Regulation 33 of the Listing Regulations. Our responsibility
is to express a conclusion on the Statement based on our review.
3. We conducted our review of the Statement in accordance with the Standard on Review Engagement
(SRE) 2410, "Review of Interim Financial Information Performed by the Independent Auditor of the
Entity" issued by the Institute of Chartered Accountants of India. This standard requires that we plan
and perform the review to obtain moderate assurance as to whether the Statement is free of material
misstatement. A review is limited primarily to inquiries of company personnel and analytical procedures
applied to financial data and thus provide less assurance than an audit conducted in accordance with
Standards on Auditing and consequently, does not enable us to obtain assurance that we would become
aware of all significant matters that might be identified in an audit. Accordingly, we do not express an
audit opinion.
4. Based on our review conducted as above, nothing has come to our attention that causes us to believe
that the accompanying Statement, prepared in accordance with the recognition and measurement
principles laid down in Indian Accounting Standard 34, “Interim Financial Reporting” (“Ind AS 34”),
prescribed under Section 133 of the Companies Act 2013, as amended, read with relevant rules issued
thereunder and other accounting principles generally accepted in India, has not disclosed the
information required to be disclosed terms of the Listing Regulations, including the manner in which it
is to be disclosed, or that it contains any material misstatement.
Emphasis of Matters
5. We draw attention to Note 3 to the Statement, which describes that, pursuant to Railway Board
Commercial Circular No. CC-60 of 2019 on increase in catering tariff for post-paid and pre-paid trains,
the Company raised demands for enhanced license fee on licensees. Certain licensees have challenged
the demands before High Courts or invoked arbitration, and awards passed against the Company in
some cases have been challenged before the Hon’ble Delhi High Court, which has stayed their execution.
As the matter is sub-judice, the enhanced license fee for the periods November 18, 2019 to March 22,
2020 (post-paid trains) and November 27, 2021 to September 30, 2026 (post-paid and pre-paid trains)
has not been recognized in the Statement for the quarter and half-year ended September 30, 2026, the
corresponding comparative periods and the year ended March 31, 2026. Our conclusion is not modified
in respect of this matter.
6. We draw attention to Note 4 to the Statement, which describes the matter relating to reimbursement
of Goods and Services Tax (GST) on the supply of Railneer to the Developer-cum-Operators (DCOs) of
four PPP Railneer plants, net of the Input Tax Credit (ITC) availed by them. As explained in the said note,
an amount of ₹ 99.32 lakhs and ₹ 192.00 lakhs has been accounted for as a claim by the Company
towards ITC for the quarter and half year ended September 30, 2026, respectively. The aggregate
amount recognized in the books of the Company towards such claim, including amounts pertaining to
